A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A and B. The appendices move from page 24 in v1 to page 25 in v3 without losing content.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation results for toy graphs, mouse interaction networks, and train scheduling in Section 3, Figures 2–8, and appendix Tables 2–3.

after.justification: v3 retains these original simulation results, including parameter recovery, calibration, posterior contraction, and travel-time distribution estimates.

M1.justification: Sections 2–3 retain the same summary-network/inference-network pipeline, four summary architectures, pooling mechanisms, and coupling-flow procedures. No algorithm or model component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same fixed-size and variable-size toy graphs, mouse microbiome-exchange simulations, and train-scheduling simulations. No dataset, task, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The toy and mouse comparisons retain DeepSets, GCN, Graph Transformer, and Set Transformer; train scheduling still uses Set Transformer alone. The added Arruda et al. citation introduces no evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The protocols remain identical, including 250-epoch toy training, 50,000 training and 1,000 validation simulations per mouse observation horizon, and 640,000 train-scheduling training samples. Metrics, preprocessing, and evaluation procedures also remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Both retain the pooling comparisons, variable-graph-size analysis in Section 3.1.4, mouse observation-horizon analysis, and train-distribution case studies. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis changes.

E5.justification: Both report five-run medians and minimum-to-maximum error bars for the toy and mouse comparisons. The 95% credible intervals, SBC confidence bands, and calibration-testing procedures are unchanged.

E6.justification: Figures 2–8 and appendix Tables 2–3 retain the same results. For example, Table 2 keeps Set Transformer/PMA loss 1.59 and lambda recovery 0.86; Table 3 keeps its five-day density/exchange-factor recovery values of 0.94/0.97.

T1.justification: The graph and permutation definitions, change-of-variables and training-loss derivations, architecture equations, metric definitions, and simulator mathematics remain unchanged. No formal result or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and summary retain the same graph-aware ABI contribution, application scope, and claims about the relative performance of summary architectures. The added background citation does not alter these claims.

C2.justification: Both retain the same interpretations of architecture performance, calibration difficulties, and reduced exchange-factor identifiability at longer mouse observation horizons. Section 4 preserves the limitations concerning small graphs, restricted graph types, and scalability.

D1.justification: Simulator specifications, feature encodings, padding, priors, network dimensions, training hyperparameters, and the code/materials access information in Section 3 are unchanged. No reproducibility details are added or removed.

R1.justification: v3 adds Arruda et al. (2025), Compositional amortized inference for large-scale hierarchical Bayesian models, to the introduction's discussion of Bayesian multilevel models and the bibliography. The broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Elizaveta Semenova's affiliation changes from Oxford Computer Science to Imperial College London's School of Public Health, and the introductory citation list and version stamp are updated. Scientific prose, section order, and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Bibliography spacing and page breaks reflow. Appendices A and B, including unchanged Tables 2–3, move from beneath the final reference on page 24 to a separate page 25. Main-text figures and tables retain their displays.

improvement.justification: v3 adds one relevant background reference and updates an affiliation, while preserving the scientific reasoning, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations. The bibliography and appendix reflow has little effect on usability, so these limited edits produce no meaningful overall quality difference.
